A.title: Apache ActiveMQ Exploit Leads to LockBit Ransomware

2: Exploitation ran a downloaded payload; privilege escalation and LSASS access followed.
3: Remote services spread payloads; a privileged service account was exposed on another host.
4: Eviction did not prevent later reentry through the unpatched service and reuse of exposed credentials.

A.caveat: The recovery snapshot is an authored counterfactual review before the reported return. It does not claim the original responders recorded these tickets.

B.title: Blurring the Lines: Intrusion Shows Connection With Three Major Ransomware Gangs

2: The process chain reached injected MSBuild, retrieved configuration and contacted external infrastructure.
3: Lateral access reached a file server; WinRAR archives were transferred with WinSCP over FTP.
4: Additional backdoors and discovery tooling were observed, but ransomware deployment was not observed before eviction.

B.caveat: Tool associations do not establish actor attribution or executed ransomware. Snapshot four precedes eviction.

C.title: Flash Alert: EtherRat and TukTuk C2 End in The Gentleman Ransomware

1: A RAMMap impersonating MSI introduced portable Node.js and obfuscated JavaScript.
2: Run-key persistence survived an initially inactive C2 configuration.
3: Stolen service credentials, GoTo Resolve, LSASS/NTDS dumping and Rclone exfiltration preceded impact.
4: Ransomware used a malicious GPO with SYSVOL/NETLOGON scheduled tasks. Arweave resolver capability was not confirmed used.

C.caveat: Implemented capability is not observed use. Provider-wide blocking is not justified by a malicious tenant or tunnel.

D.title: Another Confluence Bites the Dust: Falling to ELPACO-team Ransomware

1: Exploitation traffic targeted an exposed Confluence instance.
2: Tomcat launched commands and downloaded executable payloads.
3: Case Summary; Credential Access; Lateral Movement
Credentials, AnyDesk and remote execution enabled lateral movement to servers.
4: Ransomware followed about 62 hours after entry; widespread data exfiltration was not evidenced.

D.caveat: Small AnyDesk transfers are not proof of bulk business-data theft. Reconstructed phase order is not an exact replay clock.

E.title: Hide Your RDP: Password Spray Leads to RansomHub Deployment

1: An exposed RDP server received several hours of password spraying.
2: Successful logons led to discovery and credential harvesting.
3: RDP reached critical servers; Atera persisted, and Rclone transferred files using SFTP on port 443.
4: Ransomware spread over SMB and remote services after roughly 118 hours.

E.caveat: The first snapshot intentionally ends before successful logons. A port number alone does not establish application protocol.

F.title: From Bing Search to Ransomware: Bumblebee and AdaptixC2 Deliver Akira

1: A search for OpManager led to an impersonation site and MSI download.
2: DLL sideloading established initial access and later process injection extended it.
3: Directory credential theft, privileged accounts, RustDesk and FileZilla exfiltration preceded encryption.
4: Encryption reached the root domain before a later return into a child domain.

F.caveat: The article combines two investigations. This fixture uses the main OpManager chain only; it does not blend in the parallel BYOVD incident.

entry.proposal: Restrict unauthorized network access to entry-01, including its public entry point if present; preserve management and approved business flows. Review critical-service impact with its owner.

identity.proposal: Contain the specifically exposed or attacker-controlled account acct-01: block malicious use, invalidate sessions, and coordinate credential rotation and service dependencies with its owner.

secondary.proposal: Apply scoped network containment to compromised app-02, preserving management and essential service flows after incident commander review.

transfer.proposal: Suspend the specifically unauthorized transfer job-01 and its exact destination flow; preserve the process, transfer logs and staged data for investigation.

persistence.proposal: Disable the specifically unauthorized startup or remote-management instance rem-01 after exporting its configuration and preserving evidence.

gpo.proposal: Suspend the identified malicious policy-42 deployment and its scheduled task after preserving GPO/SYSVOL evidence; validate scope and rollback with the domain owner.

neighbor.proposal: Network-isolate the critical neighboring server neighbor-03 based on this incident.

provider.proposal: Block the entire shared cloud, SaaS and remote-management provider for every organizational user.

wipe.proposal: Immediately wipe entry-01 and delete its forensic artifacts.
